name: PYTHIA Oracle Engine
description: A FastAPI forecasting oracle ("Osiris world data in, future predictions out") found in engine/ of the Payload-Terminal-V0 repository as Python 3.14 bytecode only, with its ledger in runs/ledger.jsonl. It reads the terminal's public /api/* feeds (OSIRIS_URL) into a prose world brief, asks a local OpenAI-compatible LLM (Ollama by default, no cloud) for concrete predictions per horizon, optionally has a swarm council of persona agents deliberate and weight votes by their resolved Brier scores, persists every forecast to an append-only ledger, and later LLM-judges each forecast against the archived world to keep a scorecard. It exposes SSE and agent views for other agents and pushes outbound webhooks above probability/salience thresholds. It is a prototype whose source is not committed and whose intake targets routes the terminal has since retired; it must never be treated as canonical state or as validated risk, and its forecasts should be catalogued as proposals until the source and the intake are restored.

(Route recovered from compiled bytecode; no Python source is committed.)

capabilities.label: SSE state stream
capabilities.description: GET /state/stream opens a text/event-stream fed by the engine's async pub/sub (ping keepalives, forecast and event updates) for external agents and the UI. (Route recovered from compiled bytecode; no Python source is committed.)

capabilities.label: Consolidated machine-readable world view
capabilities.description: GET /agent/view returns one view for external agents: the assembled brief, every live event with coordinates, and current predictions. GET /agent/events returns live world events filtered by domain, source, min_salience, since (epoch ms) and limit, most-salient first, with domains_available for discovery. (Route recovered from compiled bytecode; no Python source is committed.)

capabilities.label: Current forecasts
capabilities.description: GET /predictions returns live forecasts (statement, horizon 24h|week|month|year, probability, location, lat/lng, reasoning, per-persona agent views, brief_id, resolve_after) optionally filtered by horizon and min_probability. (Route recovered from compiled bytecode; no Python source is committed.)

capabilities.label: Run an oracle pass
capabilities.description: POST /predict senses the world (reads the terminal's /api/* feeds), builds the brief, asks the local LLM for concrete predictions per horizon, optionally runs the swarm council, persists every forecast to runs/ledger.jsonl and publishes to subscribers. Returns started or "already running". Triggers LLM compute and durable ledger writes. (Route recovered from compiled bytecode; no Python source is committed.)

capabilities.label: Track record
capabilities.description: GET /scorecard returns overall Brier score, hit rate, per-horizon and per-persona accuracy, calibration bins and recent resolutions computed from the append-only ledger, where an LLM judge grades each forecast against the archived world once its horizon expires. (Route recovered from compiled bytecode; no Python source is committed.)

capabilities.label: Grade due forecasts now
capabilities.description: POST /scorecard/resolve runs a resolution pass immediately instead of waiting for the hourly ResolveLoop: LLM-judges due forecasts (bounded per pass), voids those long past their grace window, and appends resolutions to the ledger. (Route recovered from compiled bytecode; no Python source is committed.)

capabilities.label: Counterfactual forecast
capabilities.description: POST /whatif {scenario: "the Strait of Hormuz closes tonight"} asks the oracle for knock-on effects grounded in the live world; ephemeral, nothing stored, nothing enters the track record. Returns {scenario, narrative, predictions}. (Route recovered from compiled bytecode; no Python source is committed.)

capabilities.label: Ask the oracle
capabilities.description: POST /chat {message} answers a free-text question with the live sources and current predictions in context; returns {answer}. Calls the LLM; stores nothing. (Route recovered from compiled bytecode; no Python source is committed.)

capabilities.label: List and switch LLM models
capabilities.description: GET /models lists installed local (Ollama) models and the one in use; POST /model {model} switches the oracle's model at runtime. GET /swarm/models and POST /swarm/model {persona, model} read or set per-persona overrides for the swarm council (persisted to swarm_models.json). (Route recovered from compiled bytecode; no Python source is committed.)

capabilities.label: Continuous forecasting loop control
capabilities.description: /loop controls the OracleLoop (re-forecast on an interval when enabled) alongside the SenseLoop (refresh live events without the LLM) and ResolveLoop (hourly grading). (Route recovered from compiled bytecode; no Python source is committed.)

capabilities.label: Outbound webhook registration
capabilities.description: GET /webhooks lists registered hooks; POST /webhooks {url, min_probability, min_salience} registers an http(s) URL; DELETE unregisters by exact URL. After each oracle pass the engine POSTs {kind:"forecasts", ts, forecasts[{statement, horizon, probability, location, lat, lng, reasoning}]} or {kind:"events", ...} when thresholds are crossed. (Route recovered from compiled bytecode; no Python source is committed.)

capabilities.label: Forecast ledger (append-only JSONL)
capabilities.description: runs/ledger.jsonl is the engine's accountability record: kind=brief (archived top signals, at most hourly, ~500 snapshots of world memory) and kind=forecast (id, statement, horizon, probability, base_probability, location, lat/lng, reasoning, agents, brief_id, resolve_after, resolution). Hydrated at boot so live forecasts survive restart.

relations.description: Confirmed by bytecode strings: osiris_intake reads OSIRIS_URL (default http://localhost:3000) routes /api/economy, /api/markets, /api/weather, /api/infrastructure, /api/health and many retired ones (/api/conflicts, /api/gdelt, /api/fires, /api/earthquakes, /api/polymarket...) as its only world source; without the terminal the oracle has no brief. Several of those routes now answer 503 route_retired.

Inferred from bytecode in the ancestor repository, not readable source: osiris-palantir-dashboard carries the identical engine/__pycache__ (osiris_intake, oracle, swarm, ledger, webhooks, server) and its own runs/ledger.jsonl, and still serves every /api/* route the intake names (conflicts, gdelt, fires, earthquakes, polymarket) that Payload Terminal has retired behind 503. Against the dashboard's OSIRIS_URL the oracle gets a complete brief; against the terminal a partial one. Which instance is the intended world source is open.

open_questions: Where is the Python source for engine/? Only CPython 3.14 bytecode compiled on a Windows path is committed; this node is reconstructed from strings and should be re-catalogued from source.
Is the engine meant to live in this repository, in osiris-dashboard/osint-war-room, or be retired? Its intake targets 20+ terminal routes that are now 503 route_retired.
Which LLM backend, Kalshi credentials and ENGINE_PORT are intended for deployment?

corpus.holding: No corpus. Forecasts per horizon, persisted to an append-only ledger, scored later against the archived world.
